title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and executed an artifact-backed paired experiment comparing a selective low-latency verification intervention (risk scoring + fast validator) against an LLM-only baseline for LLM-generated network-change proposals. Using 400 deterministically generated operator intents (10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), generator gpt-5-mini, and a deterministic full-checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth, we observed baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975) and guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th‑percentile ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because per-stage latency telemetry was not recorded in the archived confirmatory artifacts; we disclose this gap and provide full provenance for all archived raw outputs, per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, and provider-call logs (SHA‑256 cataloged in the execution manifest). We discuss ceiling effects, the shared‑initial design and its estimand, deterministic reconciliation of planned vs observed model calls (planned_model_calls=800 under independent-generation accounting; observed model_calls_used=401 under the shared‑initial execution), and reproducible next steps.

sections.introduction: Automated intent→configuration translation promises large operator-effort savings but creates operational risk if generated proposals introduce regressions. Standard defenses use generate–validate–repair pipelines in which an LLM generates a candidate configuration, an automated verifier (digital twin / formal checker) tests functional correctness against operator-specified invariants and environment semantics, and repair or human-in-the-loop escalation follows a detected failure. Full verification is often computationally expensive and adds latency; many operational contexts therefore explore selective verification: cheaply score or approximate risk and invest heavyweight checks only where necessary. We preregistered CAND-2026-001 to answer whether a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk-scoring + fast verifier) (1) reduces unsafe commits relative to an LLM-only baseline (H1) and (2) meets a preregistered latency SLO (H2). The run was fully archived: raw LLM outputs, per-episode scorer JSONs, deterministic-validator traces, provider-call logs, task manifests, and analysis artifacts—each with SHA‑256 hashes—so every reported quantity is deterministically reproducible from the supplied artifact set. The match between preregistered design and execution (including a permitted shared-initial candidate mode) is reconciled and recorded in the execution manifest.
sections.related_work: Recent work studies LLM-driven configuration generation and repair and the integration of formal verification or digital twins into agentic NetOps workflows (representative items are included in the archived evidence bundle). Benchmarks evaluating LLM configuration repair at scale and agentic verifier-augmented architectures (Cornetto-like benchmarks; agentic configuration-repair evaluations; digital-twin validation studies) provide the experimental context. Our contribution is an artifact-backed, preregistered paired evaluation with deterministic reconciliation of provider-call accounting and per-episode validator traces; this complements prior benchmarks by prioritizing provenance and a paired confirmatory estimand under a controlled synthetic intent corpus.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and confirmatory design: We preregistered CAND-2026-001 before observing outcomes. The plan fixed the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), sampling plan (N=400 paired intents, 10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), retry and missingness rules, and analysis scripts (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The study aimed for power to detect a 5 percentage-point absolute unsafe-commit reduction with 400 pairs under conservative planning assumptions; we archived the preregistration artifact (SHA‑256 recorded). Task corpus: 400 deterministic intents were generated by a reproducible synthetic-task generator covering representative NetOps changes (ACLs, routing, interface edits). Each task manifest includes intent text, canonical required sequence, initial and expected final states, difficulty annotations, and the reference answer; representative examples and hashes are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json. Intervention and baseline: baseline = accept LLM candidate (no selective verifier); guarded = risk scorer + fast verifier applied to shared candidate per intent as preregistered (independent_condition_generation=false). We executed the permitted shared-initial design to control generator variance; details of the design choice and its implications for the estimand are documented and reconciled. Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implemented the functional checker and full scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation (per-episode JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/). Analysis: primary test = exact two-sided McNemar for paired binary outcomes with paired-bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for the paired difference. Missingness: preregistered retry policy and infrastructure-failure treatment were followed; there were no unrecovered infrastructure failures in the archived run.
sections.results: Execution and reconciliation: 400 pairs completed (complete_pair_count=400). Model calls: preregistration enumerated planned_model_calls=800 under an independent-generation accounting convention (400 intents × 2 conditions × 1 generation). The executed shared-initial design produced 401 model calls (400 shared-initial + 1 repair); this deterministic reconciliation and provider-call audit are archived in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and the execution manifest (see execution/execution_manifest.json). Confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed): baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975); guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). Paired contingency: n11=399, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Primary estimand (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Representative discordant episode: the single discordant pair (n10=1; guarded valid, baseline invalid) is archived at execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA‑256: fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA‑256: d0cbfe9a...); per-episode validator traces and provider-call logs permit stepwise replay to inspect the dependency that failed and the guarded pipeline’s repair path. Latency SLO (H2): prerergistered H2 required per-stage latency telemetry (generation, risk scoring, fast verifier, full-checker). The confirmatory artifact bundle does not include those timing traces; H2 is therefore unresolved for this run and is explicitly disclosed. All arithmetic and statistical results are reproducible from archived artifacts (analysis/ folder and execution manifest).
sections.discussion: Statistical and practical interpretation: the observed absolute gain is numerically small (0.25 percentage points) and the paired test does not reject the null (p=1.0) because the baseline was near ceiling (399/400). The paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0075] bounds the maximal plausible improvement under the observed data and preregistered analysis. Ceiling effect and power: when baseline generation performance is very high relative to the verifier’s acceptance criterion, detecting improvements requires either larger item counts or intentionally harder tasks; the preregistered corpus produced a near-ceiling baseline, limiting sensitivity to small-but-operationally-meaningful effects. Shared-initial design and estimand semantics: the preregistered execution used a shared-initial candidate per intent (independent_condition_generation=false) to control generator variance. This design changes the estimand: our confirmatory estimate quantifies the verifier/repair impact conditional on the same generator candidate, not the joint effect of independently re-sampling the generator per condition. Both conditional and joint estimands are operationally relevant in different pipelines; we preserve transparency by archiving the reconciliation and provider-call audit. Model-call accounting: planned_model_calls enumerated 800 under an independent-generation accounting convention; observed model_calls_used=401 under the shared-initial execution. The deterministic reconciliation artifact documents this difference and provides the provider-call logs for audit. Failure-mode inspection: the archived per-episode scorer JSONs and validator traces permit root-cause analysis for each failure; the single discordant episode’s traces show how the guarded pipeline corrected a candidate-level dependency violation that the baseline left intact. Reproducibility: every reported number is reproducible from archived artifacts: execution/responses/*.txt, execution/scoring/*.json, execution/provider_calls/*.json, analysis/*, and execution/execution_manifest.json. Latency telemetry missingness: the absent per-stage latency traces prevent evaluating H2; future runs must record and archive timestamps per pipeline stage to support latency claims. Operational guidance: selective verification is most beneficial when baseline generator reliability is moderate or when adversarial/OOD risk is large; with near-ceiling generators and deterministic validators the marginal safety return is small. We recommend repeat experiments with (i) independent-condition generation to estimate joint effects, (ii) larger and harder corpora (higher adversarial fraction) to expand dynamic range, (iii) multiple LLMs and validators to assess external validity, and (iv) explicit per-stage latency telemetry for H2 evaluation.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired study of a selective low-latency verification intervention for LLM-generated NetOps changes. Under the provided synthetic corpus, gpt-5-mini, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded intervention produced a small absolute safety gain (0.25 percentage points) over an already-high baseline; this difference is not statistically distinguishable from zero given the near-ceiling baseline. The preregistered latency objective (H2) could not be evaluated due to missing latency telemetry; we disclose that absence and provide the full execution provenance so that independent re-runs or extended experiments can deterministically reproduce and extend the analysis. The archived per-episode JSONs, validator traces, and provider-call logs (SHA‑256 cataloged) enable detailed failure-mode forensic work and follow-up studies targeting the open empirical gaps described above.

limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus: the deterministic generator may under-represent real operator linguistic variability and deployment heterogeneity, limiting external validity.
Single-model scope: experiments used gpt-5-mini only; results do not generalize to other LLM families without further testing.
Single deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acts as the ground-truth checker; real-device divergences or semantic gaps in the digital twin may remain.

Shared-initial design: the executed shared-initial candidate protocol yields a conditional estimand (verifier/repair effect given a shared generator candidate) different from an independent-generation estimand (independently re-sampling the generator per condition). The choice trades variance-control for a different inferential target; deterministic reconciliation artifacts document this choice.
Ceiling effect and power: the near-ceiling baseline (399/400) reduces power to detect small safety gains; future runs should use harder or larger corpora to expand dynamic range.
Missing latency telemetry: per-stage latency traces required to evaluate H2 were not archived; operational latency claims are therefore unsupported by the present artifacts.
